after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=15{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}$ is enclosed between the curve $y={x}^{2}$ and the line $y=1$ for $0\le x\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $x$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/28a3f0e1eda23169a649276a9cde34d3d96cdd75d5b2bc71c3535604612526e5.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=15{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 15{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}15{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{2}{5}{y}^{5/2}]}_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}(1-|x{|}^{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}-6{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{8}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(2-\frac{3}{4})-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{3}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2-{x}^{2}}3\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3[y]_{y=1}^{y=2-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3[2-{x}^{2}-1]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3-3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[3x-{x}^{3}]}_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =(3-1)-(-3+1) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{y}$ is enclosed between the curve $y=2-{x}^{2}$ and  the line $y=1$ for $-1\le x\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $x$-axis.
content.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/2d08bcbbcd7ec4d8c388d24728c3f3afdc7c954497f342e9ac2b459fad24e5d2.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2-{x}^{2}}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{3}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2-{x}^{2}}3\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3[y]_{y=1}^{y=2-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3[2-{x}^{2}-1]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3-3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[3x-{x}^{3}]}_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =(3-1)-(-3+1) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
